notes: Only the assigned brief, packet, notation snapshot and scan 005 images were read. No OCR, text recognition, web lookup, PDF text layer, other scan, other reader or delegation was used. The first recorded UTC time is the first image opening; the textual brief and packet had already been read immediately before it.

Coverage: every text block and every inline/display formula was read from the two halves and compared against both witnesses, including agreed prose and formulas. Half a covered the opening through the start of the derived-category remark; half b continued line by line through the final foncteur naturel, including the supplied overlap. Exactly one whole layout opening and one opening of each half were made. Each of the 22 tight crops was generated once and viewed once; no whole half was enlarged again and no locus was recropped.

All retained or resolved explicit C doubts have change entries. The remaining C-alert checks—low-left torsion 2, degree positions, formal fractions exponent, AUC order, heading capitals, Ab/cat./loc. cit., interprété, qu’ils, Soient and non unique !—are recorded in notation and coverage rather than counted as invented reading differences.

The page is a typescript with pen mathematical signs, corrections and insertion hooks. The top pen page number and lower-left pencil archive number both read 4. There are no independent diagrams or drawings. The curved strokes at non canonique, développements, Deligne, the tensor prefix and AUC G serve insertion attachment, so they are represented by inserted content rather than detached figures.

The page states that symmetries of X tensor X yield a canonical homomorphism s from pi_0 to the 2-torsion of pi_1. It then states a classification of Picard categories by pi_0, pi_1 and s up to a noncanonical equivalence, and identifies vanishing s with strictness. These are descriptions of the source, not mathematical verifications in this run.

The Remarques paragraph describes strict Picard categories through complexes in a full subcategory of the derived category of (Ab), with homology outside 0 and 1 zero. Its visible corrections move former upper degrees to lower i, 0 and 1. It asserts that the object is determined up to nonunique isomorphism by those two homology invariants. No proof or formal certificate was performed.

The page itself proposes further structure theory for nonnecessarily strict Picard categories and for (Gr)-categories, calling the developments encore dans les limbes and postponing study in the setting of champs. The empty reference brackets are left empty; Deligne is an added name, not a supplied bibliography.

Section 3 begins the universal problem of sending an AUC tensor category C into one where the images of S are invertible. It states existence of a solution denoted S^{-1}C and breaks off at le foncteur naturel. No continuation from another page was consulted.

The strongest new uncertainties relative to C are the horizontal crossbar in the old prefix beneath tout (ce ahead of co), the detached accent-like stroke over the last word of the cancelled étendus phrase (áu/au), and the absence of a detached accent in the corrected initial of eventuellement (e ahead of é). These have deliberately not been resolved by grammar.

The first K is read as an ordinary K because its upright is single and the heavy upper-right extension belongs to the superscript cancellation. The earlier dot size remains unresolved. The e under 2, E under P, old section 2, and two dots over ëxemple are sufficiently visible to remove the corresponding C uncertainty marks.

Differences already settled by a half and therefore not separately cropped here are identified as such in their change entries: opening dash, two quotation spans, and both heading underline extents. The main reader still needs personal adjudication crops for these differences. H page{4} is treated as matching page metadata; no artificial archive-number omission was counted.

H editorial notes have been compared as content: they do preserve mention of retouched indices and the word alors, so those are not treated as wholly absent. Their uncertain direction of degree movement and explicit description of alors as handwritten disagree with the visible positions and typewriter letterforms. Generic H absence of hand wrappers was not counted as an origin error.
